Rashi on Sotah 45a:10:1.hebrew: מתני' - דיליף פרט לטמון, רבי יהודה היא:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:10:1.english: Our Mishna - which derives [the law] excluding a concealed [corpse], is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:10:2.hebrew: בשדה - "ושכחת עומר בשדה", לרבי יהודה משמע "בשדה" על פני השדה, ולרבנן משמע בתוך השדה:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:10:2.english: In the field - "And you forget a sheaf in the field": according to Rabbi Yehuda, "in the field" implies on the surface of the field, and according to the Rabbis, it implies within the field.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:11:1.hebrew: התם מענייניה דקרא - צריכין למידרשיה, והכא מענייניה דקרא תדרוש ליה. גבי חלל כתיב "כי ימצא חלל" — כל היכא דמשתכח, ואפי' טמון. הלכך, על כרחך כי אתא "באדמה" למעוטי טמון בא, דתדרוש ביה "על פני האדמה", דאי לרבויי לא איצטריך:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:11:1.english: There, based on the context of the verse - [we] must expound it, and here you should expound it based on the context of the verse. Regarding a slain corpse it is written, "If a slain [person] be found" — [which implies] wherever he is found, and even [if] concealed. Therefore, perforce, when "in the land" comes, it comes to exclude [one that is] concealed, so that you expound it [as meaning] "upon the surface of the land," for if [it came] to include [a concealed corpse], it would not be needed.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:12:1.english: So too, forgetting [pertains] to revealed [sheaves] - And [it] would have excluded a concealed [sheaf] from [the verse's] plain meaning, were it not that [Scripture] subsequently included it.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:14:1.hebrew: לשכחת קמה - שאם שכח זוית אחת לקצור, קאי עלה ב"לא תשוב לקחתו", והכי משמע: "ושכחת עומר", או "ושכחת בשדה":
Rashi on Sotah 45a:14:1.english: For forgotten standing [grain] - That if he forgot to reap one corner [of the field], it is subject to [the prohibition of] "you shall not go back to take it" [Deuteronomy 24:19]. And this is what [the verse] implies: "and you forget a sheaf," or "and you forget in the field."

Rashi on Sotah 45a:14:2.hebrew: נפקא להו - מבשדך ושכחת, קרי ביה ששכח את קצת שדהו:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:14:2.english: They derive [it] - From "in your field, and you forget": read it [as meaning] that he forgot part of his field.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:15:1.hebrew: שצפו עומרין לתוך שדה חבירו - שנשבה הרוח והרימה את העומרין מן הארץ, והציפתן לתוך שדה חבירו, ושכחן כסבור שאינן שלו. נפקא מ"בשדך", ולא בשדה חבירך, דלא הוו שכחה:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:15:1.english: That sheaves floated into another’s field - That the wind blew and lifted the sheaves from the ground, and floated them into another’s field, and he forgot them, thinking that they were not his. [This] is derived from “in your field” — and not in another’s field — that they are not [classified as] forgotten [sheaves].

Rashi on Sotah 45a:15:2.hebrew: ורבנן - מיעוטא דשדה חבירו נפקא להו מדהוה ליה למכתב "כי תקצור קצירך בשדה ושכחת", וכתיב "בשדך":
Rashi on Sotah 45a:15:2.english: And the Rabbis - The exclusion of another's field is derived by them from [the fact] that it could have written, "When you reap your harvest in the field and forget," yet it is written, "in your field."

Rashi on Sotah 45a:16:1.english: Sheaves floated into his field - That they were lying upon a stone, or a pillar, or one upon another.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:17:1.english: Excludes [sheaves] that floated - And it enters your mind [that] they actually floated upon a stone or upon a pillar.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:18:1.hebrew: וליטעמיך לתוך שדה חבירו - צפו על גבי אבן הוא דמעיט, אבל מונחים לא מיעט? והא "בשדך" כתיב! אלא הא דקאמר צפו, לאו דוקא צפו על שום דבר קאמר, דאפי' מונחים על גבי קרקע נמי קאמר "אינו שכחה"; והאי דקאמר צפו, דלא משכחת עומרין לתוך שדה חבירו אלא בצפו, שהרוח מצפתן על הארץ ומביאתן לשם:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:18:1.english: And according to your reasoning, into another's field - [Is it only where] they floated on top of a stone that [the baraita] excluded [from being deemed forgotten], whereas [where they are] resting [on the ground] it did not exclude [them]? But "in your field" is written [in Scripture]! Rather, when it says "they floated," it does not specifically mean floating on top of something, for even [when they are] resting on the ground it also says "it is not [deemed] forgotten"; and the reason it says "they floated" is because you do not find sheaves [entering] into another's field except by floating, as the wind causes them to float over the ground and brings them there.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:20:1.hebrew: שהחזיק בו להוליכו לעיר - ס"ד השתא דאורחא דמילתא נקט, ולאו דוקא:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:20:1.english: That he took hold of to take it to the city - We presently assume that [the baraita] stated the usual case, and not specifically.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:21:1.hebrew: זכה ביה - ותו לא הוי שכחה, דבעינן שכוח מעיקרו, כדאמר בב"מ בפרק קמא (דף יא.):
Rashi on Sotah 45a:21:1.english: He acquired it - And it is no longer [considered] a forgotten sheaf [shikchah], for we require [that it be] forgotten from the outset, as stated in Bava Metzia in the first chapter (11a).

Rashi on Sotah 45a:22:1.hebrew: מפני שהוא כצף - שהוא פטור על שהחזיק בו, כאילו היה עודנו צף מעל הקרקע ומונח בידו:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:22:1.english: Because it is like [it is] floating - That it is exempt [from the law of forgotten sheaves] because he took possession of it, as if it were still floating above the ground and resting in his hand.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:23:1.hebrew: הריני כבן עזאי בשוקי טבריא - יום אחד היה דעתו צלולה, אמר: הריני כאן בפומבדיתא מוכן להשיב דבר לשואל בעומק ובחריפות, כבן עזאי שהיה חריף ודורש בשוקי טבריא:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:23:1.english: I am hereby as ben Azzai in the markets of Tiberias - One day his mind was clear, [and] he said: I am hereby here in Pumbedita, ready to answer a matter for [any] questioner with depth and sharpness, like ben Azzai, who was sharp and expounded in the markets of Tiberias.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:23:2.hebrew: שני חללים זה על גב זה - והאחד משוך להלן מחבירו מעט, ואם תמדוד מזה יקרב לעיר אחת; ואם תמדוד מחבירו יקרב לעיר אחרת:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:23:2.english: Two slain [people] one on top of the other - And one extends slightly beyond the other, and if you measure from this one, it will be closer to one city, and if you measure from the other, it will be closer to another city.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:25:1.hebrew: ולא מזה מודד כו' - וה"ה דמיבעיא ליה נמי: או דלמא מין במינו לא הוי טמון, מין במינו לא הוי צף, ומשניהם מודד, אלא שהוא בכלל אלו:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:25:1.english: And he does not measure from this [one], etc. - And the same applies that he also asks: "Or perhaps a substance [in contact] with the same [type of] substance is not [considered] concealed, [and] a substance [in contact] with the same [type of] substance is not [considered] floating, and he measures from both of them," except that it is included in these [other possibilities].

Rashi on Sotah 45a:2:1.english: Clearly [near] to a city - In the open, and [it is] obvious that there is no city as close as this [one].

Rashi on Sotah 45a:3:1.hebrew: מתני' - דלא קתני מלך וכהן גדול, דלא כר' אליעזר בן יעקב:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:3:1.english: Our Mishnah - which does not teach a king and a High Priest, is not in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:4:1.hebrew: אי כרבי יהודה - חמשה, אי כרבי שמעון - שלשה, ולא בעי כולה סנהדרין:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:4:1.english: Either in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - five [Elders], [or] in accordance with Rabbi Shimon — three, and he does not require the entire Sanhedrin.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:5:1.hebrew: מצאן זקן ממרא - לב"ד הגדול, שאינו נעשה ממרא אלא בב"ד של שבעים ואחד, כדיליף בפרק קמא דסנהדרין:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:5:1.english: A rebellious elder found them - [Referring to] the Great Court, for he does not become a rebellious [elder] except [before] the court of seventy-one [judges], as is derived in the first chapter of Sanhedrin.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:5:2.hebrew: אבי פאגי - כל שהוא בתוך היקף החיצון של ירושלים קרוי בי פאגי, ולי נראה שהוא לשון חבישה, כמו שקורין ציגל"א (צינגל"א: חומה של עיר, כמו חמור ובית פאגי (ב"מ דף ט.), בשטדידור"א — בית ראש של אפסר קורין כן:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:5:2.english: In Bei Pagei - Whatever is within the outer perimeter of Jerusalem is called Bei Pagei. And to me it appears that it is an expression of binding, just as they call tzigla (tzingla): a wall of a city; like "a donkey and its beit pagah" (Bava Metzia 9a), bestedura — the headpiece of a halter is called so.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:5:3.hebrew: והמרה עליהן - כלומר, על מה ששאל מהם שם ואמרו לו ההלכה, הלך לעירו והורה לעשות כדרך שהיה מורה בתחילה, דהוה ליה ממרא על פיהם:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:5:3.english: And he rebelled against them - That is to say, regarding what he asked of them there and they told him the halakha, he went to his city and ruled to act in the manner that he had ruled originally, whereby he is [considered] one who rebels against their word.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:5:4.hebrew: המקום - המיוחד למשפט, והוא לשכת הגזית:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:5:4.english: The place - [That] which is designated for judgment, and it is the Chamber of Hewn Stone.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:6:1.hebrew: דנפיק מינייהו כמה - לבי פאגי, דאיצטריך לאשמועינן דפטור משום טעמא דחוץ לב"ד:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:6:1.english: How many of them went out - to Beit Pagei, that it was necessary to teach us that he is exempt because of the reason [of being] outside the court.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:6:2.hebrew: דלמא הנך דאיכא גוואי כוותיה סבירא להו - ומהיכא תיתי לן חיובא, דאיצטריך קרא למיפטריה:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:6:2.english: Perhaps those who are inside hold in accordance with him - And from where would we have liability [for him], that a verse would be needed to exempt him?

Rashi on Sotah 45a:7:1.hebrew: שררך - זה סנהדרין שיושבת בטיבורה של א"י:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:7:1.english: Your navel [shorerekh] - This [refers to] the Sanhedrin, which sits at the navel [i.e., center] of the Land of Israel.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:7:2.hebrew: אגן הסהר - שעשויין כחצי לבנה עגולה בשורת ישיבתן, כדי שיהו כולן רואין זה את זה:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:7:2.english: A round goblet - For [the Sanhedrin] are arranged like half of a round moon in the row of their seating, so that they may all see one another.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:7:3.hebrew: המזג - כשיעור מזג, שני חלקים מים ואחד יין, ואף כאן צריך שישתייר שליש:
Rashi on Sotah 45a:7:3.english: Mingled wine - Like the measure of mingled [wine] — two parts water and one [part] wine — and here too, a third must remain.

Rashi on Sotah 45a:9:1.english: It is taught like Rav Yosef - Who said [that] Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov requires the entire Sanhedrin.
